title: Engine oil & filter change
tools: Ramps or a trolley jack and axle stands
parts: 4.5 L of 0W-20 (or 5W-30) API SN/ILSAC oil – 4.3 L is needed
Oil filter (club-listed 15601-76008; check against your frame number)
steps: Run the engine for a few minutes so the oil is warm, not hot. Park on level ground, handbrake on, engine off.
Raise the front on ramps, or jack it up at the proper lifting point and support it on axle stands. Never work under it on the jack alone.
Take the oil filler cap off so the oil drains freely.
Put the tray under the sump, undo the drain plug and let it drain fully (10 minutes or so).
Clean the plug, fit a new washer, and refit it firmly. Don't over-tighten into the aluminium sump.
Move the tray under the filter and unscrew it. Some oil will run out.
Wipe the filter mounting face. Smear clean oil on the new filter's rubber seal, screw it on until the seal touches, then about another ¾ turn by hand.
Lower the car so it's level. Pour in about 3.8 L, wait a minute, then check the dipstick.
Top up a little at a time towards 4.3 L until the level is near the top mark. Don't overfill.
Refit the filler cap. Start the engine and let it idle for a minute; the oil light should go out within seconds. Look for leaks at the plug and filter.
Switch off, wait at least 5 minutes, then re-check the dipstick and top up if needed.
Reset the maintenance reminder if one is set, and log it in My Car.
warnings: Hot oil burns. Let it cool if you've just driven far.
Take used oil to the council tip; it's illegal to pour it away.

title: CVT fluid drain, fill and level check
tools: Ramps or jack and stands (car must end up level)
24 mm socket and a long extension (filler bolt)
6 mm hex key/bit (drain and overflow tube)
Fluid pump or long funnel and tube
Wire jumper for the OBD socket
Thermometer or OBD reader that shows CVT temperature (useful)
parts: Toyota CVT Fluid TC (or FE on later cars) – about 4–5 L per drain & fill; 10–12 L for a thorough change
steps: Get the car level and safely supported. The level check only works if the car is level.
Undo the 24 mm filler bolt first. If you drain it and then can't open the filler, you're stranded.
Remove the 6 mm hex drain plug and let it drain into the tray. Expect about 1.5 L at first.
Undo the overflow tube inside the drain hole (also 6 mm hex). Another 0.5–1 L comes out. Roughly 2–4 L in total, which is only part of the 8.7 L in the system.
Refit the overflow tube and drain plug, and fill with the same amount of new fluid through the filler hole.
To change more of it: start the engine, move slowly through P-R-N-D with your foot on the brake, then drain and refill again. Repeat until the fluid coming out looks clean.
Level check, fluid must be 35–45 °C: start cold and slightly overfilled. With the ignition on and the A/C off, then ignition off, bridge OBD pins 4 and 13 with the wire.
Start the engine. Move the selector N→D→N→D quickly (under 1.5 s each) until the D light stays on for 2 s. That's fluid-temperature mode. Remove the jumper and go back to P.
D light off = too cold, wait. D light flashing = too hot, let it cool and start again. D light steady = in the window.

With the D light steady and the engine running, remove the drain plug. Let the excess run out of the overflow tube until it just drips, then refit the plug with a new gasket. If nothing comes out, it's low: add fluid and redo the check.
Refit the filler bolt with a new gasket. Test drive, and look for leaks.
warnings: Use CVT fluid only. ATF will damage the CVT.
On very high-mileage cars with original fluid, some garages advise doing one drain & fill at a time over a few weeks rather than changing everything at once.

title: Smart key battery
tools: Small flat screwdriver with tape round the tip
steps: Slide out the mechanical key blade.
Gently prise the cover apart at the slot. The taped tip stops it scratching.
Take out the old cell and fit the new one + side up.
Clip the cover back together and refit the blade.
Press a button. The LED on the key should light.
warnings: Keep coin cells away from children. Swallowing one is extremely dangerous.

title: Checking and replacing a fuse
tools: Fuse puller (in the engine bay fuse box)
parts: Spare mini fuses of the right ratings
steps: Turn the power switch off.
Find the right fuse in the Fuses section of this app. There are 2 boxes under the bonnet (3 on the hybrid) and one in each front footwell.
Pull the fuse with the puller and look at the metal link. A gap or blackening means it's blown.
Fit a fuse of exactly the same rating.
If it blows again, there's a fault in that circuit. Get it looked at rather than fitting a bigger fuse.
warnings: Never fit a higher-rated fuse or bridge a fuse holder. That's a fire risk.

title: Changing a wheel
steps: Stop somewhere safe and level, hazards on, handbrake on, P selected. Get passengers out and well away from traffic.
Chock the wheel diagonally opposite.
Loosen the wheel nuts half a turn while the tyre is still on the ground.
Jack the car up at the correct jacking point (see the owner's manual diagram) until the tyre clears the ground.
Remove the nuts and the wheel. Fit the spare, then run the nuts on by hand, tapered side towards the wheel.
Lower the car and tighten the nuts in a criss-cross pattern to 103 N·m (76 lb·ft).
Space-saver spare: 420 kPa (61 psi), keep to low speeds, and get the proper tyre refitted soon.
Re-check the nut torque after a short drive.
warnings: Don't use the car's jack with anyone under the car. For maintenance use a garage jack and axle stands at the proper lift points.

title: Power sliding door won't open or close properly
parts: Possibly a door cable or motor assembly
steps: Check the 12 V battery first. Low voltage is a common cause of power doors misbehaving. Charge it or test it (12.4 V or more at rest).
Check the PSD RH / PSD LH and ECU-B fuses (see Fuses).
Try a reset: disconnect the battery negative for a minute, reconnect it, switch the power door main switch on, then open and close the door fully with the button.
Listen while operating it. Motor runs but the door doesn't move → probably a broken cable. Silence from the motor → the motor, its wiring, or a fuse.
Door stops partway or jams → often a worn outer sheath on the cable, binding in the pulley system, or dry runners.
Clean the door runners and lightly grease them. Some owners also put silicone grease on the cable drum splines when refitting.
Cable replacement is a big job (owners report about 4 hours). Get the right part for your frame number and follow a video for your generation.
warnings: Keep hands clear of a power door. It can close with real force when it's re-learning its travel.

title: Removing the centre dash and audio unit
tools: Masking tape to protect the trim
steps: Disconnect the battery negative if you'll be unplugging the audio or nav.
Unscrew the gear knob.
Ease off the cluster panel around the gear lever. It's held by about 21 clips, so work round it gently with trim tools.
Unclip the air-con control panel (4 clips).
Unclip the audio surround panel (9 clips).
Undo the 4 screws holding the audio bracket.
Pull the audio unit and bracket forward and unplug it.
Refit in reverse. Seat every clip fully before pressing the panels home.

notes: The source sheet's + and − marks for each speaker pair didn't survive translation. Check polarity with a meter or the original PDF before wiring.
Cars with the Toyota Premium Sound (18-speaker) or Panoramic Super Live Sound (11-speaker) systems use a different integrated unit and can't take a standard aftermarket head unit.
Colours can vary with year and grade.
warnings: The cluster panel has a lot of clips. Pull evenly and never lever against the dash itself.

title: Front and rear door trim & speaker removal
tools: Rivets or M5 screws to refit
steps: Front door: unclip the small cover behind the door mirror (2 clips and a hook).
Unclip the door pillar cover (3 clips).
Unclip the cover behind the interior door handle (3 hooks) and remove the screw behind it.
Remove the screw under the door pull, then unclip the door grip (3 hooks).
Unclip the power window switch panel (9 hooks) and unplug it.
Remove the last screw, then pop the trim off its 12 clips and lift it off the window ledge. Unplug anything still attached.
The front speaker is riveted in: drill out the 4 rivets with a 5 mm bit (they can't be reused) and lift the speaker out.
Rear sliding door: remove 1 screw, then unclip the trim (15 clips, 5 hooks). The speaker comes out after 3 screws.
Refit in reverse. Secure the front speaker with new rivets or M5 screws and nuts.
notes: Front speaker mounting depth is about 61 mm and rear about 52 mm (from Alpine's measurements). Useful when choosing replacements.
